subject: Operator access attestation + escrow approach for MedSys on-prem deployment
messages:
From: Ava Lopez <ava.lopez@medsys.com>
To: chloe_martin@redwoodinference.com
Cc: Dr. Priyanka Rao <prao@medsys.com>
Date: 2026-11-01T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Operator access attestation + escrow scenario — MedSys on-prem

Hi Chloe,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As we move toward a Private (on-prem) deployment for the pilot, Legal and Security have surfaced two items they need to close before we can sign the Order Form: 1) a clear attestation and control path for any Redwood operator access during audits/incident support, and 2) an escrow-like mechanism for model runtime artifacts / manifests so we can validate code provenance in a future audit.

Can you propose concrete options (both contractual and operational) that would satisfy MedSys requirements? High level asks from our side:
- No persistent operator credentials in our environment; any operator access must be scoped, logged, and auditable.
- If Redwood needs to ship snapshots or binaries for escrow/verification, we need a verifiable checksum + chain-of-custody.
- Prefer an escrow agent or neutral custodian for any long-term artifact storage.

Id like to loop in Legal now (ccd) so we can align on acceptable language in the MSA addendum. Do you have a proposed timeline?

Best,
Ava Lopez
Director, IT Security
MedSys Health
From: chloe_martin@redwoodinference.com
To: Ava Lopez <ava.lopez@medsys.com>
Cc: Dr. Priyanka Rao <prao@medsys.com>, karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2026-11-01T11:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Operator access attestation + escrow scenario — MedSys on-prem

Ava,

Thanks for outlining the asks. Below are three pragmatic options weve used with other regulated customers; each pairs an operational control with a contract clause we can bake into an MSA addendum or Order Form. Ill attach templates for attestation and our proposed escrow flow.

Option A — On-site witnessed access + signed attestation (lowest privilege):
- Redwood engineers granted access only when requested; access performed on-site (customer-provided workstation) or via a customer-managed jump host in the VPC.
- Customer security witnesses the session and signs a short attestation after completion.
- Contract: include a short \"On-site / Witnessed Access\" clause and a requirement for a signed session attestation.

Option B — Escrowed snapshot + hashed manifests (medium):
- Redwood deposits a time-stamped snapshot (runtime artifact + manifest) with a neutral escrow agent. Snapshot includes SHA256 manifests and a signed metadata file from Redwood.
- During audits, MedSys can retrieve snapshot from escrow and validate checksums against runtime environment.
- Contract: escrow agent agreement + chain-of-custody clause; responsibilities and retrieval SLA defined in addendum.

Option C — Limited remote operator with strong telemetry (operational + audit trail):
- Short-lived operator accounts created via customer-managed identity provider (SAML/OIDC) with just-in-time elevation; all sessions recorded and immutable audit logs (WORM storage) shipped to MedSys for retention window.
- Contract: detailed access-window and telemetry-retention commitments, plus indemnity carve-outs for misuse.

Weve attached: operator_attestation_template.docx (editable), escrow_flow_v2.pdf (diagram), and a short runbook excerpt describing commands wed allow for remote diagnostics. If youd like, I can have Legal propose precise redline language today and send back for your review.

Timeline: if we get alignment on approach by EOD Wednesday, we can produce a draft addendum within two business days.

Regards,
Chloe Martin
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
chloe@redwoodinference.com
Attachments: operator_attestation_template.docx (docx), escrow_flow_v2.pdf (pdf)
From: karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com
To: chloe_martin@redwoodinference.com
Cc: Ava Lopez <ava.lopez@medsys.com>, neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2026-11-01T14:20:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Operator access attestation + escrow scenario — MedSys on-prem

Chloe / Ava,

I reviewed the operational options Chloe proposed. From a contracting standpoint, here are recommended redlines we think will cover MedSyss risk envelope while keeping implementation feasible:

1) \"Operator Access\" definition: limit to specific, named roles (e.g., \"Tier-2 On-call Engineer\") and require explicit, time-bound approvals.
2) \"Audit Evidence\" clause: Redwood will provide SHA256 manifests and a signed metadata file for any escrowed artifact; retrieval requires 3 business-day notice except for emergency audit (24h).
3) Escrow custodian: allow either (a) a mutually agreed neutral escrow agent, or (b) Redwood-operated escrow with third-party notarization (signed manifest + timestamp authority).
4) Liability and indemnity: carve out willful misuse; include joint inspection process and an agreed SRM for dispute escalation.

Ive attached a markup of the MSA and a proposed addendum template (redlines_msa_markup.docx). Ava / MedSys Legal: please confirm whether you need a third-party escrow agent as a hard requirement or if notarized Redwood escrow is acceptable. Also confirm acceptable retrieval SLAs.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Sr. Counsel, Contracts & Commercial
Redwood Inference
Attachments: redlines_msa_markup.docx (docx)
From: Legal (MedSys) <legal@medsys.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com, chloe_martin@redwoodinference.com
Cc: Ava Lopez <ava.lopez@medsys.com>, Dr. Priyanka Rao <prao@medsys.com>
Date: 2026-11-02T08:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Operator access attestation + escrow scenario — MedSys on-prem

Karthik / Chloe,

Thanks for the fast turnaround. A few clarifying points from MedSys Legal / Compliance:

- Escrow agent: MedSys strongly prefers a neutral third-party custodian for long-term storage of snapshots; Redwood-operated escrow with notarization is a fallback but will require additional audit rights.
- Operator access: remote operator access is acceptable only if access is brokered by a customer-managed jump host and MFA is enforced. No persistent operator keys.
- Audits / Retrieval: retrieval windows must be contractually guaranteed (we propose 48 business hours for standard audit retrieval; 8 hours for emergency with an escalation path).
- Attestation: we need a standard attestation template that includes the list of artifacts provided, signature-by-role, and a timestamp authority.

Please share the updated addendum with the escrow agent options spelled out, and a clean attestation template we can circulate internally. Weve attached a short questionnaire outlining our minimum documentation items (MedSys-Attestation-Questions.pdf).

If possible, please also provide the HubSpot deal link and a single point-of-contact for procurement and SOW execution so our vendor team can trigger the procurement pipeline.

Regards,
MedSys Legal
legal@medsys.com
Attachments: MedSys-Attestation-Questions.pdf (pdf)
From: chloe_martin@redwoodinference.com
To: Legal (MedSys) <legal@medsys.com>, Ava Lopez <ava.lopez@medsys.com>, karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2026-11-02T12:01:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Operator access attestation + escrow scenario — MedSys on-prem

Team,

Appreciate the clarity. Proposed next steps and commitments from Redwood:
1) Escrow approach: well present two documented options in the addendum: (i) neutral escrow agent (recommended), or (ii) Redwood-hosted escrow with cryptographic notarization (signed manifest + timestamp authority). We will include retrieval SLAs: standard 48 business hours, emergency 8 business hours.

2) Operator access: Redwood confirms no persistent operator credentials. Remote access only via customer-managed jump host or on-site; short-lived, SAML/OIDC-bound elevation and full session recording. Sessions will be shipped to customer in WORM storage for retention period specified in addendum.

3) Attestation template: attached is a clean attestation template (operator_attestation_template.docx). We will sign attestation responses for any witnessed sessions; VP Engineering will sign formal attestations for escrow snapshots.

4) Contract redlines: Karthik will publish a clean addendum draft and a tracked-redline MSA for your review within 24 hours.

HubSpot / procurement contact: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/98721 (deal RDW-98721). Procurement POC: Neha Kapoor (neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com).

If that aligns, Ill trigger DocuSign for the addendum and share the link here. Thanks — happy to jump on a 30m call if Legal prefers to walk through scenarios end-to-end.

Best,
Chloe Martin
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
chloe@redwoodinference.com
Attachments: operator_attestation_template.docx (docx)
